featured_reviews.name: Shirish Salaskar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this note as a genuinely disappointed and frustrated customer who trusted one of the world’s biggest technology brands and invested in a so-called “premium flagship” smartphone — the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 5, costing ₹1,65,000.

When someone spends this kind of money on a mobile phone, they are not buying just a gadget. They are buying reliability, trust, durability, and long-term support.

Unfortunately, my experience with Samsung has been the complete opposite.

Under normal usage, without any physical damage, water exposure, or misuse:

• The inner fold display failed once and had to be replaced.
• Recently, after installing an official Samsung software update and restarting the device, the outer display suddenly developed a permanent vertical green line.

This defect appeared immediately after the update, which raises a serious question:
How can a software update damage a hardware display in a premium device?

When I approached the authorized Samsung service center, I was informed that since the phone is now technically “out of warranty”, I must pay again for display replacement, even though this is the second major display failure in the same device.

This leads to a very simple but painful reality:

I paid ₹1.65 lakh for a phone that cannot survive normal usage, and now I am expected to keep paying more every time its most critical component fails.

For this price, one can literally buy a motorcycle. Yet the durability and after-sales experience of this phone feels worse than many mid-range smartphones.

Instead of taking responsibility, the support system keeps:
•	Delaying the case
•	Closing and reopening references
•	Giving generic replies
•	Avoiding a clear written resolution

There is no accountability for product quality, no ownership of repeated defects, and no meaningful support for a premium customer.

This experience has taught me a hard lesson:
Innovation without reliability is not progress — it is just an expensive experiment, and the customer becomes the test subject.

Based on my personal experience, I would strongly advise consumers to think very carefully before buying any Samsung Fold series phone. The concept looks futuristic, but the long-term reliability and service support do not justify the extremely high price.

A premium brand should deliver premium durability and premium responsibility — not premium disappointment.

This is not just about one phone.
This is about trust, value, and consumer rights.

And unfortunately, in my case, Samsung has failed on all three.
